_note: Record is the Health Passport. Its §26 paths keep their names and are mounted under /v1/record by reference; the P0 service answers most of them already, in development, on synthetic data, on loopback. Share links, their opening and revocation, and the export are built at P1 (Wave 4) in the same service, and version one of the link and the export are withdrawn; the Record engine's settings are answered by the engine runtime. The HL7 v2 inbound path is a supplier's, so it is a door to add rather than a route. Every read goes through the consent gateway.
_encounterStatusesNote: The resource is encounter-statuses and not encounters. A field ending Ref is read as a reference into the store of the engine that declares its resource, so declaring encounters here would make every frozen encounterRef on Care's and Clinical's routes a reach into the record's store, which they are not: they carry the reference and the entry stays in the record.

doorsToAdd.why: ADT, ORU and ORM messages from partner systems are supplier callbacks. §26 names the path /hl7v2/inbound; it is mounted as a door with mutual TLS per partner, not answered as a route.

A claim's diagnosis coding is assembled inside the record and clinical boundary from the signed encounter and handed to the switching partner through this door. Money records the billing side and never holds the coding.

It named no grant for the link to ride on, so nothing tied its scope, purpose or end to a decision the patient had made, and nothing refused a scope wider than that decision; it had no field for the link's secret, which is what opens it; and its two refusals were all it refused, with no word for a link to a payer, a link past the grant ceiling or a sealed category without a tick. It offered an IPS document and a PDF nobody has built, and it answered with a reference to an export kept for collection, a copy of the whole record at rest that no store holds.
